importance_ranking.reason: MS Portable Toilets have significant visual variation across sub-types — single cabin vs multi-compartment block vs trolley-mounted vs container type — and buyers use the image to immediately confirm structure type, build quality, and finish before reading any text. Wrong structure type or visibly poor build quality causes an immediate skip.

Buyers shortlist based on No. of Seats, Toilet Seat type (Indian/Western), and Structure Type before contacting sellers — these specs define whether the product matches the site requirement and cannot be inferred from image alone.

Price varies substantially with No. of Seats, structure type, and included fittings — Indian B2B buyers (especially contractors and government procurement) compare prices aggressively across listings once spec equivalence is confirmed, making price a primary shortlisting lever.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant nationally recognised brand exists in the MS portable toilet cabin market — buyers search by spec, price, and location of manufacturer, not by brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: For government tender and bulk contractor procurement, seller credentials (manufacturing capability, past supply track record, GST registration) matter during vendor evaluation but are checked after spec and price shortlisting.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Per sq ft quoting exists for custom/modular configurations but per piece is the dominant and universally understood transaction unit for standard cabin units — no buyer confusion arises.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied for a finished cabin structure — no buyer questions whether a portable toilet cabin is sold per piece.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Seat count is the primary price driver and non-interchangeable product class separator — a 1-seat labour toilet and a 16-seat toilet block serve entirely different site requirements and carry vastly different prices.
Indian vs Western commode type is non-interchangeable for the end user and drives a meaningful price and fitment difference — buyers specify this upfront and cannot substitute one for the other.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Footprint dimensions (e.g. 3x3 ft, 4x6 ft) determine site space allocation and transportation logistics — contractors and government buyers specify this as a primary requirement alongside seat count.

MS tubular frame gauge or section size (e.g. 40x40 mm, 2mm thickness) is a key quality and durability differentiator that affects price and buyer confidence in structural integrity for long-duration site deployment.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Seat count defines the scale of the sanitation requirement and is the single most important routing signal — sellers need this to determine whether they can supply the right product class and to price accurately.
Indian vs Western commode type is non-interchangeable and must be confirmed upfront — sellers configure the unit differently and buyers cannot substitute one for the other on site.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Construction site, event, government/municipal, or defence camp usage drives different compliance, durability, and fitting requirements — sellers need this to confirm product suitability and quote the right configuration.
